decisions.summary: Added PANOPTICON_TMUX_SOCKET_NAME as a validated tmux socket override so tests can run against a throwaway tmux server instead of the shared panopticon socket.
Hardened the agent-spawning integration fixture with a per-run isolated tmux socket and a stub claude binary so accidental real tmux session creation cannot launch the real Claude CLI.

hazards.summary: The workspace already had unrelated dirty files before implementation: .panopticon/projects.yaml and several .claude/rules files.
hazards.mitigation: Do not stage unrelated pre-existing files in the PAN-1808 bead commit; stage only tmux/test changes plus the required continue-state update.

hazards.summary: If a test process changes PANOPTICON_HOME or the tmux socket override, a process-global one-shot tmux-context guard can otherwise keep stale prepared state.
hazards.mitigation: Track the prepared tmux context by socket name and config path so changing either value prepares the correct isolated context.

resumePoint.description: PAN-1808 implementation is coded and typecheck, lint, and full npm test passed. Next commit only the scoped PAN-1808 files, close bead workspace-n240x, push, and run pan done.

sessionHistory.note: Implemented isolated tmux socket injection, hardened agent-spawning tests with a stub claude binary and throwaway socket cleanup, added socket override tests, ran targeted npm test invocation plus npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and full npm test, and confirmed no leaked agent-pan-resume-redeliver session on the shared panopticon socket.
